name: BWX Technologies

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (BWX Technologies logo.svg), saved as the 500 px PNG rendering Wikimedia serves because the SVG download was rate-limited (429) at the time

description: BWXT designs and builds the nuclear reactors, fuel and precision components for US Navy submarines and aircraft carriers under the DOE/NNSA Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program; its Government Operations segment, about three quarters of revenue, is built around that work, and the 10-K calls competition for it limited because of technical, regulatory and security barriers. A smaller Commercial Operations segment makes heavy components such as steam generators for nuclear power plants, provides nuclear services and engineering (expanded by the May 2025 Kinectrics purchase) and produces medical radioisotopes. It also holds stakes in joint ventures that run US nuclear weapons sites and cleanup projects, which show up as equity income rather than revenue, and is developing advanced reactors for NASA, the Pentagon and the DOE. Backlog reached $8.4 billion on June 30, 2026.

gics.note: Wikipedia 'List of S&P 400 companies', raw wikitext read 2026-10-27: BWX Technologies, Industrials, Aerospace & Defense. The list gives only sector and sub-industry, so industry group and industry are left null.

hq.note: Cover page of the FY2025 10-K: 800 Main Street, 4th Floor, Lynchburg, VA 24504

employees.note: About 10,400 worldwide: 6,700 US, 3,500 Canada, about 200 elsewhere (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Government Operations
businessLines.how: The US Government pays under long-term contracts to design and build naval reactors, components and fuel (the Navy's March 2024 30-year shipbuilding plan shows sustained or higher submarine and carrier procurement); the site-operation joint ventures earn fees tied to performance scores, booked mainly as equity income.
businessLines.description: Naval nuclear reactors, components and fuel for the DOE/NNSA Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program; uranium processing and downblending; research-reactor fuel; advanced reactor design for NASA, the Department of War and the DOE; management and operation of US government sites through joint ventures; valves and fittings for naval and commercial shipping.

operatingProfit.note: 87.2% of total segment operating income of $452.6M before unallocated corporate of $(48.1)M

businessLines.name: Commercial Operations
businessLines.how: One-off large equipment orders (steam generators, storage containers) from nuclear utilities, plus recurring in-plant service and engineering work around outages, and sales of medical isotopes and radiopharmaceutical products.
businessLines.description: Commercial nuclear steam generators, heat exchangers, pressure vessels, reactor components, fuel, fuel-handling systems and spent-fuel storage containers; in-plant nuclear engineering and maintenance services; Kinectrics (acquired May 20, 2025) lifecycle services for nuclear power and transmission and distribution; medical radioisotopes, radiopharmaceuticals and contract manufacturing for life-science customers.

operatingProfit.note: 12.8% of total segment operating income of $452.6M

brands.name: Joint ventures operating US government sites (Lawrence Livermore, Los Alamos legacy cleanup, Savannah River, Pantex, Hanford, Paducah, West Valley, Strategic Petroleum Reserve and others)
brands.share: Equity income of investees $74.9M in FY2025 (Government $72.6M, Commercial $2.3M) versus $55.9M in FY2024; revenue of the ventures is not consolidated
